subject.title: feat: Automatic model routing based on message type

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a generic core turn-routing policy for model capability and intent, or keep specialized routing in provider/plugin-owned integrations until a minimal shared hook is defined?
rationale: The request adds persistent configuration and changes dispatch semantics across providers and sessions; source evidence shows model capability metadata and primary/fallback selection, but not an existing owner-approved policy for selecting among specialized models per turn.

options.title: Design a narrow generic capability fallback
options.body: Define an explicit opt-in attachment-capability fallback contract and leave text classification and TTS routing out until they have separate semantics.

options.title: Add a plugin routing seam first
options.body: Expose a stable pre-dispatch extension point so provider or user-owned plugins can make specialized routing decisions without Xiaomi-specific core configuration.

options.title: Keep manual selection only
options.body: Decline automatic routing for now and retain the existing primary-model plus error-fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow generic capability fallback
recommendation.body: Define an explicit opt-in attachment-capability fallback contract and leave text classification and TTS routing out until they have separate semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter is the only identified contact who can clarify the intended distinction between attachment routing, ASR, and TTS; current-main history did not establish a code owner in this review.
